slides.texte_overlay:
Things you should stop
doing as a friend
Stop only texting when you need something. A random "Saw this and thought of you" means more than you think. Friendships die from silence, not from big fights.
Stop cancelling at the last minute. Once is life. Every week is a message. If you can't make it, say so early, and suggest another date in the same message.
Stop turning every story into your story. When a friend shares something, ask a second question before you share yours. Being heard is the rarest gift you can give.
Stop keeping score. Who paid last, who called last, who invited who. Good friendships aren't a balance sheet. Give a little more than you take and stop counting.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll bring new stories to every catch-up, and your friends will notice the difference.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll bring new stories to every catch-up with friends.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop staying quiet when they're making a mistake. A real friend says "I'm not sure that's a good idea" once, kindly. Then respects their choice whatever happens.
Stop forgetting the big days. Birthdays, new jobs, anniversaries of hard moments. Put them in your calendar. Showing up on the days that matter is what real friends do.
